script.title: The paint rulebook the bombs missed

lines: A researcher searched hard for German navy camouflage records.
Ships have worn camouflage since ancient times.
In the Second World War, the German Navy used a whole mix of paint schemes.
They kept changing.
The researcher wanted to explain them all in one English book.
Nobody had written a full one in English before.
But the proof was scarce.
Allied bombers had destroyed many German navy records.
Written sources were even harder to find.
Then two editions of the building rules survived.
Both came from the naval shipyard at Wilhelmshaven.
They ran from November 1941 to July 1944.
They were a great help to the book.
Thanks to them, English readers finally got a full guide.
Even so, a reviewer urged caution.
Paint quality varied greatly.
You see, it is like a cake recipe.
Two bakers follow one page.
One uses bad flour, and the cakes look different.
On the ships, what was actually achieved was often quite different from the standard.
So the surviving rulebook shows the plan, not always the ship.

claims.claim: Locating sources for the work was difficult and written primary sources were even harder to come by.
Camouflage on ships dates back to the ancients and has been used ever since.
In the Second World War the German Navy used a myriad of camouflage schemes and styles that appear to have been continually changing.
Volume 1 of German Naval Camouflage is the first comprehensive work on Kriegsmarine camouflage practices for the English-reading world.
Many Kriegsmarine records were destroyed during the Allied bombing campaign, making official records scarce.
Two editions of the General Building Regulations Nr. 31, ranging from November 1941 to July 1944 and used by the Kriegsmarinewerft Wilhelmshaven, survived and were a great help.
Paint quality varied greatly, and what was actually achieved was often quite different from the camouflage standard.

cast.researcher: a 45 year old woman historian with shoulder-length auburn hair with silver streaks, round tortoiseshell glasses, an olive green cardigan over a cream blouse
cast.painter: a 50 year old broad-shouldered German shipyard painter with grey stubble, a flat cap splashed with paint and blue overalls stained with grey paint, 1940s
cast.reviewer: a 55 year old man with a bald head, a neat grey goatee, a navy blazer and a red bow tie
cast.baker: a 30 year old woman baker with black curly hair under a yellow headscarf, brown skin, a white apron over a teal shirt
cast.reader: a 70 year old man with wild white hair, bushy white eyebrows, a brown corduroy jacket and a red scarf
